title: google-research/paper-orchestra — PaperOrchestra is a multi-agent framework for automated AI research paper writing.
content:
PaperOrchestra is a multi-agent framework for automated AI research paper writing. It flexibly transforms unconstrained pre-writing materials (ideas and experimental logs) into submission-ready LaTeX manuscripts, including comprehensive literature synthesis and generated visuals, such as plots and conceptual diagrams.
Acting like an orchestrated team of specialized agents, it handles outline generation, literature review, section writing, content refinement, and plotting to close the gap between raw research materials and submission ready papers.
- Multi-Agent Pipeline: Orchestrates specialized agents (Outline, Literature Review, Section Writing, Content Refinement, Plotting) for end-to-end paper generation.
- Comprehensive Literature Synthesis: Automatically searches, prioritizes, and integrates relevant literature into the manuscript.
- Visuals Generation: Generates plots and supports the inclusion of conceptual diagrams.
- LaTeX Automation: Produces submission-ready LaTeX manuscripts adhering to target conference templates.
- Environment Setup: The project relies on a Conda environment named paper_orchestra. You can set up a similar environment with Python 3.11 and install the required dependencies.
conda create -n paper_orchestra python=3.11 conda activate paper_orchestra pip install -r requirements.txt
- Environment Variables: Create a .env file in the root of the project and add your API keys:
# Add keys if you have them, otherwise leave them empty # You need to specify related keys if you want to use the model # For example, if you want to use Gemini models, you need to specify either VERTEX_AI_PROJECT and VERTEX_AI_LOCATION, or GEMINI_API_KEY # If you want to use OpenAI models, you need to specify OPENAI_API_KEY SEMANTIC_SCHOLAR_API_KEY=your_semantic_scholar_api_key OPENAI_API_KEY=your_openai_api_key VERTEX_AI_PROJECT=your_vertex_ai_project VERTEX_AI_LOCATION=your_vertex_ai_location GEMINI_API_KEY=your_gemini_api_key # if you want to run demo and send emails to yourself at the end, set these 2 fields as well SMTP_EMAIL=your_email SMTP_PASSWORD=your_password
The dataset used for paper generation is not included in this code repository. It will be released separately at a later date.
Once available, you should download the dataset and place it under the datasets/ directory.
You can run the paper generation pipeline using the provided bash script or directly via the Python CLI.
./paper_writing_cli.shpython paper_writing_cli.py \
  --raw_materials_dir /path_to_your_raw_materials/ \
  --latex_template_dir /path_to_your_latex_template/ \
  --output_dir /path_to_your_output_folder/ \
  --use_plotting true
- --raw_materials_dir: (Required) Directory containing the raw materials (e.g., idea and experimental log).
- --latex_template_dir: (Required) Directory containing the LaTeX template (e.g., templates/cvpr2025).
- --output_dir: Directory to output the generated paper. If not specified, an automatic folder with a timestamp is created.
- --use_plotting: Enable the plotting agent workflow to generate figures from code (Default: False).
- --writer_model_name: LLM for writer and literature agents.
- --reflection_model_name: LLM for reflection agents.
We provide an interactive Streamlit demo for the paper generation pipeline. For instructions on how to run and use it, please refer to the README.md in the frontend directory.
- autoraters/: Contains scripts for automated evaluation.
- methods/: Core logic for agents and pipeline execution.
- templates/: LaTeX templates for target conferences, you can add your own template by creating a new subfolder under this directory.
- utils/: Utility functions for API calls, PDF handling, etc.
If you find this repo or our paper helpful, please cite it as follows:
@article{song2026paperorchestra,
  title={PaperOrchestra: A Multi-Agent Framework for Automated AI Research Paper Writing},
  author={Song, Yiwen and Song, Yale and Pfister, Tomas and Yoon, Jinsung},
  journal={arXiv preprint arXiv:2604.05018},
  year={2026}
}
This is not an officially supported Google product.

report.summary: Google Research's PaperOrchestra is an open-source multi-agent framework that turns raw ideas and experimental logs into submission-ready LaTeX AI research papers, complete with literature review and generated figures.
report.background: Large language models have moved steadily from drafting paragraphs toward automating entire research workflows. Systems such as Sakana AI's 'The AI Scientist' and various AutoML-plus-writeup pipelines showed that agents can propose experiments and produce drafts, but outputs often lacked proper literature grounding, conference formatting, or publication-quality visuals. Meanwhile, academic publishing faces mounting volume pressure, reproducibility concerns, and heavy formatting overhead that consumes researcher time. PaperOrchestra, released by Google Research researchers Yiwen Song, Yale Song, Tomas Pfister and Jinsung Yoon, targets the last mile: the gap between messy pre-writing artifacts (an idea note plus experimental logs) and a polished manuscript. It reflects a broader industry pattern of composing specialised agents—planner, retriever, writer, critic, plotter—rather than relying on a single monolithic prompt. Notably, it is explicitly labelled 'not an officially supported Google product', signalling an exploratory research release rather than a production service.
key_points: The system is a pipeline of specialised agents: Outline, Literature Review, Section Writing, Content Refinement and Plotting. Each agent hands off to the next, mimicking how a human team divides drafting, citation gathering, editing and figure production. Users configure separate models for writing agents and 'reflection' (self-critique) agents, so cheaper or stronger LLMs can be mixed.

Literature synthesis is automated rather than manual. Using a Semantic Scholar API key, the Literature Review agent searches, prioritises and integrates relevant prior work into the manuscript. This addresses a common failure of naive LLM drafting—plausible-sounding but ungrounded or fabricated citations—by anchoring references to a real scholarly index.

Output is conference-ready LaTeX. Papers are generated against templates stored under templates/ (for example templates/cvpr2025), and users can add their own by creating a subfolder. A plotting agent, enabled with --use_plotting, writes and executes code to produce figures and supports conceptual diagrams.

Running it is straightforward but key-dependent. It needs a Conda environment with Python 3.11, a requirements.txt install, and a .env file holding SEMANTIC_SCHOLAR_API_KEY plus either GEMINI_API_KEY or Vertex AI credentials, or OPENAI_API_KEY. Optional SMTP settings let the demo email the finished PDF to you.

Evaluation and data remain partly gated. An autoraters/ folder provides automated scoring scripts and a Streamlit frontend offers an interactive demo, but the dataset used for paper generation is not in the repository and is promised for a separate release, so out-of-the-box benchmarking is limited.
report.impact: For the AI industry, PaperOrchestra is a clear signal that agent orchestration—not single-model capability—is becoming the unit of product design in research automation, and Google Research is seeding open tooling for it. For developers, the repo is a readable reference architecture: role-specialised agents, a reflection loop, tool calls to a scholarly API, code-executing plotting, and template-driven LaTeX rendering, all reusable in adjacent document-generation domains. For regular users, notably students and early-career researchers, the appeal is speed: turning scattered notes into a structured draft with citations and figures. But the risks are real. Automated manuscripts could flood conferences with low-novelty submissions, strain peer review further, and blur authorship norms. Because the system writes from your logs, it inherits your errors—and citation relevance still needs human verification. Expect the debate over disclosure policies to sharpen.
report.tools: Watch the PaperOrchestra repository itself (methods/, templates/, autoraters/, and the Streamlit frontend), which is the quickest path to experimenting. Pair it with Semantic Scholar's API for grounded citations and LaTeX/Overleaf for final polish. For comparison, study Sakana AI's AI Scientist and open agent frameworks such as LangGraph or AutoGen, which make similar multi-agent pipelines easy to build. Keep a citation checker and a plagiarism/AI-detection pass in your workflow before submitting anything.
